At which point my computer will start to freeze, well why should you be worried anyways? Well, there are couple of reasons. For example, high temperatures can reduce life span of your hardware, others for example can reduce cpu clock in order to maintain stability or eventually risk of breaking down. Okay, that sounds scary right? What do i need to know first? Well first we need to know the term ''TJunction". TJunction is a term which means that manufacturer put a safety limit, when that limit is passed, cpu/gpu will underclock itself in order to maintain itself from destruction. In the older days, pc would just shut down, but now, component will just underclock itself by default, that means if you have a cpu that is clocked at 3.2GHz, it will go as down as its lowest multiplayer for example 9.

For example TJunction for AMD Radeon R290x is 95 celsius, and AMD is saying that users should not worry, well i would be worried if my card would hit that mark.

TL:DR> there is no optimal temperature for your components. You dont have minimum but you have a bare maximum. Well, you just need to keep your compoments under TJunction limit that is all.
